correctness.rationale: Directly grouping output coordinates modulo p gives p blocks formed from two unit vectors, proving the exact 1±inner-product-modulus spectrum. The cyclic boundary is explicitly treated and produces the sum k0. The integer phase map has determinant ±2, so for odd q its image is all residue words and for even q precisely the even-parity words, with multiplicity two. Counting these words proves the survival law at every threshold, including singularity. An antipodal-letter bound plus the same parity condition gives the sharp optimum, all equality cases and counts. Finite exhaustive tests over p=2..5, q=2..8 and independent full matrix eigenvalue tests up to p=7 corroborate the analytical derivation; they are not the proof.

value.rationale: A uniformly distributed finite alphabet is a natural implementable model for digital time-frequency sampling. The theorem gives exact failure probability at every dimension, not just bounds, and determines the exact maximum worst-case reconstruction stability and when orthonormality is feasible. The divisibility-by-four transition and odd-p binary impossibility are structural arithmetic obstructions that disappear in continuous-phase models; optimizers and their counts are explicit. It is restricted to a natural square two-translation design, not claimed as a universal Gabor theorem.
